newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian c.bank sees '96 CPI at 13.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Latvian c.bank sees '96 CPI at 13.5 pct.

text.p: Latvia's central bank on Wednesday forecast 1996 inflation at 13.5 percent, followed by a drop to between 10.5 and 11.0 percent in 1997.
It also said most monetary indicators reflected stabilisation in 1996 after a 1995 bank crisis.
Central bank chief Einar Repshe also predicted 1997 GDP growth between 3.0 and 3.5 percent but said lending needed to grow.
Deposits in banks rose 27.0 percent to 560 million lats in 1996 while credits granted were unchanged at 230 million lats.
"The results were more optimistic than forecast by the media," central bank deputy head Ilmar Rimshevic told a news conference.
"The most satisfactory thing for the Bank of Latvia was the passing of the balanced budget for the first time in the history of Latvia," Rimshevic added.
IN December, parliament passed a deficit-free budget that came after an expected 40 million lat deficit in 1996.
"In 1997, every person will benefit from the actions that we and the government began last year," Rimshevic added.
Repshe stressed that banks should lend more and said the central bank's priority would be to stimulate lending to manufacturing companies.
"Latvian exports have good potential. We can look into the future with cautious optimism," Repshe added.
Latvia was hit by a bank crisis in mid-1995 that helped slow down the economy and cause the budget deficit to swell to 90 million lats.
A recovery began in 1996 and GDP is expected to be around 2.5 percent as interest rates have fallen.
"I am convinced that the government will cope with fulfilling the balanced budget," Repshe said.
